title: Returned-Payment Fee on the Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreement: Ledger Posting Card
content:
**Policy entry.** When the bank returns a payment on a Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreement for insufficient funds or because the account is closed, one returned-payment fee is posted against that returned payment, dated with the due date of the billing period the payment was for. A card chargeback carries no returned-payment fee at all. Posting the fee raises the agreement's balance due by the fee, and the tenant sees it on the ledger, the statement and the new balance due.

## Which returns carry the fee

| Reason the payment came back | Returned-payment fee |
|---|---|
| returned by the bank for insufficient funds | one fee, posted against that returned payment |
| returned by the bank because the account is closed | one fee, posted against that returned payment |
| card chargeback | none |

## Posting tool

The fee is posted with the agent-side tool `post_unit_returned_payment_fee_fb0d77c5`, which the agent unlocks and then calls. One call adds one returned-payment fee entry to the agreement's ledger, dated today, tied to the returned payment it arises from and to the due date of the billing period that payment was for.

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `rental_id` | the storage unit rental agreement number, read from the rental agreement lookup | identifier |
| `reference_entry_id` | the ledger entry number of the payment the bank returned — the payment entry the reversal points at — read from the agreement's ledger lookup | identifier |
| `period_start` | the due date (first day) of the billing period the returned payment was for, exactly as that period's rent charge shows it on the ledger | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `fee_type` | the kind of fee posted | enum, one value: `returned_payment_fee` — the fee charged when the bank returns a payment unpaid |
| `amount` | the returned-payment fee to post, in US dollars | 2 decimal places, always positive; more places are rounded to the cent |

**Return.** The call succeeds when the receipt returns the new ledger entry number: `entry_id` (the new ledger entry number), `rental_id` (the agreement charged), `fee_type` (the kind of fee posted), `reference_entry_id` (the returned payment the fee is posted against), `amount` (the fee posted, US dollars to 2 decimal places), `entry_date` (the posting date, today) and `balance_due` (the agreement's balance due after the fee).

## Reading the contract

- `reference_entry_id` names the original payment entry, not the reversal entry that points at it.
- The tool lands the entry with the values passed; it does not figure the fee.
